summary: Alexandr Wang describes Meta's Muse Spark 1.3 as an update over Muse Spark 1.2 with better reasoning and coding, fewer tool calls, fewer tokens per task, and improved long-horizon requirement retention.

mechanisms.reason: The post states a specific reduction in tool calls and tokens needed per task, indicating less compute per unit of output for the new model version.
mechanisms.quote: uses ~20% fewer tool calls, ~25% fewer tokens

practices.reason: An engineer building on Muse Spark could expect fewer tokens and tool calls per task and better reasoning/coding performance, though the comparison is the lab's own unreplicated claim.
practices.quote: It's a step up on reasoning and coding. compared to Muse Spark 1.2, Muse Spark 1.3 wastes fewer turns, uses ~20% fewer tool calls, ~25% fewer tokens, and holds onto requirements well during long-horizon tasks.
